hook: The popular Nine Realms map of Norse mythology is actually a modern, non-ancient invention.

sections.voiceover: The popular Nine Realms map of Norse mythology is actually a modern, non-ancient invention.
sections.visual_cue: A digital map of the cosmos dissolving into static.

text_overlay.text: Nine Realms map: A modern myth

sections.voiceover: The poem Völuspá mentions 9 worlds existing within Yggdrasill, the mythological tree of the cosmos. Where did this organized structure actually come from?
sections.visual_cue: Ancient parchment illustration of a tree.

sections.voiceover: Scholar Eldar Heide proves the Æsir, or Norse gods, occupied many conflicting locations across history.
sections.visual_cue: Portrait of a scholar overlaid with ancient text fragments.

sections.voiceover: Heide found pre-Christian sources scattered the Æsir across the east, west, sky, and sea. Yggdrasill shows the cosmos was fluid, not a vertical stack of 9 distinct worlds.
sections.visual_cue: Animated diagram showing shifting, non-hierarchical points.
b_roll: Abstract representation of sea and sky

sections.voiceover: Discard the structured map, as ancient Norse sources provide no definitive list of locations.
sections.visual_cue: The tree Yggdrasill fading into a simple, unmapped horizon.
